Maya (Procurement): Hey team, got a quote back from RateBridge for the inference-billing pilot. Numbers look ... dense. Can we sanity-check before I reply?
Owen (Finance): share the PDF? main asks: commit vs overage rates, invoice cadence, proration, and trial credit terms.
Maya (Procurement): attaching the summary I made (see pasted table below). Quick Q: they quoted "embedding unit" per 1k vectors — is that normal? :thinking_face:
Priya (Eng): embeddings per 1k vectors is usual. But we bill by token for gen, and by vector count for embeddings. Need a conversion example for our usage.
Carlos - RateBridge: Hi all — Carlos from RateBridge. Happy to clarify. Our embedding SKU is per 1k vectors; generation is per 1k tokens. Pilot offer includes $5k credit, 3-month commitment option (optional), and post-commit overage at 120% of committed rate. We invoice monthly net-30. Data retention: 30 days by default, enterprise add-on for 365 days.
Sam (PM): 3-month commit is short — will that lock price? If we scale faster, can we increase capacity mid-term?
Carlos - RateBridge: Price lock for the committed amount only. You can scale; additional usage billed at overage rate. We can add scheduled increases to the commitment with prorated pricing for the remainder of term.
Owen (Finance): Need clarity on proration: if we increase commitment mid-month, do we prorate both billing and credits? Also what happens on early termination? Any termination fees?
Carlos - RateBridge: We prorate any commitment increases. Early termination: standard 30 days notice; for committed discounts we invoice a catch-up equal to the discount applied on the fulfilled portion (i.e., you pay back the discount proportionally).
Priya (Eng): For cost modeling, here's a small usage sample from our staging month: 
```
requests,avg_tokens_per_request,avg_vectors_per_request
12000,220,6
```
Priya (Eng): If RateBridge counts embeddings per-1k vectors, and gen per-1k tokens, how do we compute blended cost?
Carlos - RateBridge: Example calc: embeddings billed = ceil(total_vectors/1000) * rate_per_1k_vectors. Generation billed = ceil(total_tokens/1000) * rate_per_1k_tokens. For your sample: total_vectors = 12000*6 = 72000 -> 72 units; total_tokens = 12000*220 = 2,640,000 -> 2640 units.
Owen (Finance): Can you provide the unit rates as numbers for the pilot quote? We need to plug into our cost model. Also, does the $5k pilot credit apply to overage or only to committed spend?
Carlos - RateBridge: Pilot unit rates (pilot pricing): embeddings = $0.90 per 1k vectors, generation = $0.015 per 1k tokens. $5k pilot credit applies to total invoice (both commit and overage) until consumed; unused credit does not roll beyond 90 days.
Maya (Procurement): Thanks — added to the spreadsheet. Two procurement asks: 1) can they extend data retention to 365 for pilot (temporary) and 2) can we get net-45 invoice term with PO?
Alex (Legal): Also need standard CPRA clauses and export/data deletion commitments in writing for pilot. Can RateBridge provide a DPA addendum?
Carlos - RateBridge: We can add a 365-day retention toggle for pilots. Net-45 for customers with PO is doable — needs procurement approval. DPA: yes, we have a standard DPA and can redline on CPRA items.
Owen (Finance): One more — how are embedding dimensionality changes handled? If we increase vector size (e.g., 1536->2048), will counts change for billing?
Carlos - RateBridge: Billing based on number of vectors, not dimensionality. If you change model and vectors per request change, counts adjust accordingly.
Priya (Eng): Good. Also: what about billing for cache hits? We have prefix/KV caching — do cached responses still count?
Carlos - RateBridge: Cache hits are not billed as generation, unless you still request vectorization on-demand. For matched cached outputs we won't bill generation tokens, but we may bill minimal request handling fees for high-throughput API calls (usually negligible).
Sam (PM): Next steps: Maya to ask for written pilot addendum with unit rates, credit terms, net-45 PO option, 365-day retention toggle, and DPA. Also schedule a short vendor demo for rate-limiting and invoice reporting UI.
Maya (Procurement): I'll draft and ask for the addendum. Carlos, can you send a calendar link for a 30-min demo next week? Prefer mornings PST.
Carlos - RateBridge: Sending calendar link in DM now.
Owen (Finance): I'll take the unit-rate numbers and run a 6-month projection. Ping me if you need a modeled CSV.
Alex (Legal): I'll wait for the DPA. Quick ask: any SOC2 or ISO certs?
Carlos - RateBridge: We are SOC 2 Type II in progress, ISO27001 planned for Q4. I'll attach SOC2 report once available.
Priya (Eng): :+1: If demo covers API keys, SSO/SCIM, and billing export (CSV or BigQuery sink), we're set.
Maya (Procurement): Great — thanks everyone. I'll share the draft reply + addendum when ready.
Sam (PM): Heads-up: procurement needs approval window ~5 business days after addendum. Targeting pilot start in ~3 weeks. :eyes:
